weakest_scene.visible_evidence: seg3:start–end: one flat teal square fills the frame with '29400T' in the middle and a tiny overlapping 'NASA's Cold Atom Lab (ISS)' label. Data perches on top doing nothing.
weakest_scene.root_cause: An area/scale machine was fed a distance comparison in mangled units (29400T, presumably trillion miles), so one value fills the frame and the other is invisible. Nothing depicts 'far away vs 250 miles up'.
weakest_scene.repair_goal: Show the distance as a journey: Earth with the ISS just above it at 250 miles, while the Boomerang Nebula sits at the end of an absurdly long zoom-out. Data rides or launches the Cold Atom Lab to orbit, and one readable label in plain units ('5,000 light-years' vs '250 miles') lands by mid-beat.
